name: Biting Tongues
label: Factory Records
lede: Biting Tongues started as live music for a silent film at Tony Wilson's Factory club, never played the same set twice, and ended in the same studio sessions that gave birth to 808 State.

eras.title: Live music for a silent film
eras.text: Biting Tongues began as a soundtrack played in the room, under a 16mm film, at the Factory club in Hulme. The five-piece that settled in 1980 took its cues from Sun Ra, Miles Davis, Funkadelic, Can and This Heat, and from cheap Impulse reissues turning up in Manchester shops, not from three-chord punk.

years.cap: Biting Tongues at the Manchester Film & Video Workshop, 1979
years.src: Biting Tongues: History · LTM: Biting Tongues
years.h: A silent film needs a band, so Walmsley, Hollings and Sherwood form one
years.p: [[Howard Walmsley|ffcb095e-0055-4bc9-928f-aafaefff2bfb]] had shot a 16mm silent film called Biting Tongues. With [[Ken Hollings|35bb3a06-e935-4608-8af8-891db9998fcd]] and Eddie Sherwood he played music under it at [[Tony Wilson|124a6f5d-b2e0-4a75-95ad-db4c38063e02]]'s Factory club, the Russell Club in Hulme.
years.xp:
[[Colin Seddon|e66d7fb5-1998-4d42-a5ed-db88e3c6e721]] and [[Graham Massey|6739352a-3f16-418b-ba43-6c41912badc5]] came in from their own project, the Post Natals. The early lineups shifted from show to show before the five-piece settled around June 1980.

Getting ready for a gig meant making Xerox posters, slides and super-8 film, cutting tapes of random sound, writing texts and working out choreography, as well as writing the music.

years.big: Typewriters, sheet metal, animal bones, plastic ray guns
q: Never do what's easy: never make it look difficult.
years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues · Biting Tongues: History
years.h: No set ever repeats, and nobody gets an encore
years.p: Biting Tongues wrote new material for each show and used whatever it had brought on stage as instruments. When the material ran out, the night was over.
years.xp:
LTM's history lists the props: typewriters, engraving tools, sheet metal, animal bones and plastic ray guns. Hollings delivered texts rather than sung lyrics, and the band refused encores because there was nothing left to play.

Massey's version of the early sound: "All noise is good - fill in all the gaps."

years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues · Manchester Digital Music Archive: Biting Tongues
years.h: Don't Heal comes out on Situation 2
years.p: Recorded at Drone in Chorlton (August 1980) and Pennine (January 1981) on New Hormones money, it was played straight through with random tapes mixed in.
years.xp: LTM says it was recorded and mixed in a single afternoon, with very few overdubs.

years.cap: Inserts from the Live It cassette, New Hormones, 1981
years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues
years.h: Live It, a six-track cassette for New Hormones
years.p: Three of the tracks went live straight to a two-track master, and LTM calls it closer to how the band sounded on stage than Don't Heal.
years.xp: Massey remembered New Hormones as "much more of a family record company", run by Richard Boon and Peter Wright out of a shared house. Factory, later, would feel very different.

eras.title: Libreville, and Tony Wilson's money for a feature
eras.text: The band made its most focused album and then a 55-minute film, with Wilson paying the final bill. By the end of it, two of the five founders were gone.

years.cap: Flyer for Biting Tongues at the Barracuda, London, February 1982
years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues · Biting Tongues: History
years.h: Libreville is recorded at Bootleg Studio
years.p: Belgian producer Roland Beelans was involved. The album had a New Hormones number, ORG 26, but New Hormones ran out of money before it came out.

years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues
years.h: Libreville lands on Paragon instead
years.p: Paragon issued it as Virtue 1. LTM calls it more focused than anything the band had recorded before.

years.cap: Biting Tongues at Band on the Wall, Manchester, 1983
years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues · Biting Tongues: History · Manchester Digital Music Archive: Biting Tongues
years.h: Wilson puts up the money for Feverhouse
years.p: Hollings wrote it, Walmsley directed and Massey appears on screen. The 55-minute film was shot through 1983, with Tony Wilson supplying the final funding.
years.xp: The film came out through Factory's Ikon video arm, and its soundtrack became a Factory album. LTM notes that the post-production support Wilson promised never arrived.

years.src: Biting Tongues: History · LTM: Biting Tongues · Wikipedia: Biting Tongues
years.h: Hollings leaves, Sherwood goes to Simply Red, Phil Kirby takes over the drums
years.p: By 1984 Hollings felt the project had outgrown working as a collective. Eddie Sherwood joined [[Simply Red|a9100753-f539-43cf-bcc9-579566fb512e]], and Kirby brought what LTM calls high octane, jazz-influenced drumming.

eras.title: On Factory, with nobody in their corner
eras.text: Biting Tongues finally put records out on Factory itself, just as the label's attention was going to New Order. The lineup kept turning over, and its engine room left for Yargo.

years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues
years.h: The Feverhouse soundtrack becomes FACT 105
years.p: Loops and an AMS digital delay carry it. The film came out on video as Ikon 10.
years.xp: Massey on the approach: "A conscious effort to keep the guitar/drums/bass convention out." The soundtrack runs about the length of the film, 55 minutes.

years.src: Biting Tongues: History · LTM: Biting Tongues · Wikipedia: Biting Tongues
years.h: Factory's first Biting Tongues EP is cut in Bury and Ancoats
years.p: Trouble Hand, FAC 134, was recorded at Square One in Bury and Out of the Blue in Ancoats, with Mark Derbey now on bass. Seddon had left to start Inner Sense Percussion Ensemble.

years.cap: Flyer for Biting Tongues at the International, Manchester, December 1985
years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues
years.h: "There was no one who was championing us," Massey says of Factory
years.p: Next to New Hormones' family feel, Factory seemed taken up with [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]]'s success. Walmsley was puzzled that the label spent heavily on sleeves while querying producers' fees.

years.cap: Advert for Kalima and Biting Tongues at the International, Manchester, December 1986
years.src: Biting Tongues: History · LTM: Biting Tongues
years.h: Patrick Steer, Yargo's bassist, replaces Derbey; Tom Barnish adds trombone
years.p: John Hurst was by now treated as a member too, running the band through a digital delay and harmonizer from the desk.

years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues
years.h: Compressor points the band toward MIDI
years.p: FAC 188, out on 7-inch and 12-inch. Massey had been through a recording course at Spirit Studios, and the band was moving toward MIDI and electronics.
years.xp: Ikon followed it with Wall of Surf, a 50-minute video collection.

years.cap: Earthbeat festival poster, Sefton Park, Liverpool, August 1987, with Biting Tongues and Yargo on the bill
years.src: Biting Tongues: History · Wikipedia: Biting Tongues
years.h: Kirby and Steer leave to do [[Yargo|a14f7175-2d12-46fc-9079-cd05079e38fd]] full time
years.p: Yargo had signed to London Records. Basil Clarke, who had sung with Biting Tongues, was Yargo's singer.

eras.title: Same sessions, two bands
eras.text: The last Biting Tongues album and the first 808 State album came out of the same studio time. 808 State took off; Recharge stalled at test pressings.

years.src: Biting Tongues: History · LTM: Biting Tongues · Wikipedia: Biting Tongues
years.h: Massey starts [[808 State|36f35db0-bc09-43e7-8650-a123224943c7]] while finishing Recharge
years.p: Massey formed 808 State with Martin Price, Darren Partington, Andy Barker and [[A Guy Called Gerald|b343730d-a34e-44d5-9191-a83f00231716]], and recorded Quadrastate in the same sessions as Biting Tongues' Recharge.
years.xp:
The overlap left fingerprints. Massey on 808 State's Pacific State: "If it wasn't for the fact of Howard leaving his soprano sax in the studio overnight, Pacific State might have been another story."

Walmsley kept making films and videos, including some for 808 State.

years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues · Wikipedia: Biting Tongues
years.h: Love Out goes to the clubs; Cut Deep folds before Recharge
years.p: The single featured guest singer Denise Johnstone. Recharge got as far as promos and test pressings, which became, in LTM's words, a holy grail for early 808 State fans.

eras.title: The original five, twenty years on
eras.text: LTM put the catalogue back out and the founding lineup played again, first at the ICA, then in Salford and Brussels.

years.src: Biting Tongues: History · LTM: Biting Tongues
years.h: Massey, Hollings, Walmsley, Seddon and Sherwood play the ICA
years.p: The original five reunited for a one-off at the ICA in London, on a bill with [[Crispy Ambulance|3420e6bc-8551-4c6c-86ca-c13a3115edd3]]. After rehearsing, Massey said they still sounded like themselves.

years.src: Wikipedia: Biting Tongues · Manchester Digital Music Archive: Biting Tongues
years.h: Recharge gets an official release, fourteen years late
years.p: LTM issued the album that Cut Deep never could, part of a run of LTM releases that brought the band's catalogue back.

years.cap: Biting Tongues at Islington Mill, Salford, February 2007
years.src: LTM: Biting Tongues
years.h: Back on stage at Islington Mill, Salford
years.p: The founding five played again, at the Salford studio and arts space, per LTM.

years.src: Manchester Digital Music Archive: Biting Tongues
years.h: Clear Your Screens collects live recordings
years.p: Released on Touch and Tapeworm, a live compilation from the band's years on stage.
